item.content:encoded:
Hidden AGI watch · Sat 7 November 2026

Nov 7: no probability moved. PSI says its system, using a non-public Anthropic model, proved a long-open conjecture; W2 is met, with no post-Astra release or outside evaluation listed.

Corrections
  • We said The JOLTS hires rate averaged 2.1% over June-August 2026 in Information (bls:JTS510000000000000HIR; 1.6% in August, tied with October 2023 as its lowest reading since January 2017 apart from April 2020) ... Measured against each industry's own 2017-2019 average, we find Information 16 points and Professional and business services 4 points behind the average of Construction, Health care and Leisure and hospitality ..., which puts Information at the bottom edge of its 2017-2019 range on this comparison and Professional and business services inside it. (Also: the sector's hires rate fell to 1.6% in August 2026, below its 2017-2019 range of 2.4% to 3.5%.). That was wrong (corrected 5 November 2026): With the September data released on November 3, 2026, BLS revised Information's August 2026 hires rate to 2.5% (bls:JTS510000000000000HIR), inside its 2017-2019 range of 2.4% to 3.5%, and Professional and business services' to 4.3% (fred:JTS540099HIR). By our calculation on the revised data, Information's June-August average is 2.4% and about 6 points behind the comparison industries, inside its 2017-2019 range on that measure, and Professional and business services is about 3 points behind, also inside its range, so Information did not reach the bottom edge of its range in August (data.bls.gov).
  • We said The BLS nonfarm business labor share (FRED PRS85006173, index 2017=100) was 93.446 in the second quarter of 2026, down from 96.723 a year earlier and 97.871 in the first quarter of 2025, ... while output per hour (OPHNFB) rose 2.2% over the year. (J9's reason: the share fell for a fifth straight quarter to 93.4 in the second quarter of 2026.).
